translated.evidence: After completing the English version data expansion, we translated the data into 22 other languages. For Basic Questions, given the large volume of 795 items, we used LLM-based translation with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet, followed by native speaker review and correction. For the 47 Instructions, we used professional human translators who were native speakers of the target languages and proficient in English.

native_annotators.evidence: All personnel we hired for instruction data translation and dataset quality control were native speakers of their respective languages, and they possessed near-native English proficiency. Original data collected via questionnaire from 31 respondents including researchers, native speakers, and linguistics experts. However, Basic Questions were LLM-translated with native speaker review, not fully natively authored.

culturally_grounded.evidence: The benchmark is translated from English and focuses on instruction-following mechanics (format, keywords, length, punctuation, etc.) rather than culturally-specific content. The Basic Questions were originally collected in English and expanded using English-language LLMs. While translations were reviewed for naturalness, the tasks test format compliance rather than cultural knowledge.

MaXIFE.annotation_quality_notes: Three-round quality control: (1) content rationality and accuracy, (2) language expression naturalness reviewed by native speakers, (3) parallel consistency across language versions. Human-model evaluation consistency rates: 97.3% (high-resource), 95.2% (medium-resource), 94.6% (low-resource).
